scope: Audited isolated campaign fragment runner only; all entries are partial implementations, not quest certification
notes: Quest lifecycle Start/Stop/Reset are explicitly rejected by the runner.
Journal operations, nested stages, globals, read-only reference queries and visibility mutations are subsets; complete engine lifecycle, world effects and client acceptance remain open.
Condition support is limited to stage-log contexts and specific flags/run-on types.

Stage-log GetIsAliasRef (566) compares exact campaign reference identities on explicit Reference or QuestAlias selectors. Its first parameter is a signed nonnegative owning-quest alias ID, including zero, never a FormID. QuestAlias selectors independently use the signed ID at byte 28. Proven empty reference aliases compare false; missing aliases, location aliases, unsupported fill/effects, missing private copies and cross-phase targets still fail. Populated endpoints use tracked campaign reference reads. Implicit subjects, other run-on selectors, special flags and non-stage execution remain unsupported; alias-fill/lifecycle dependencies remain missing capabilities. This does not add GetIsID or certify the tutorial quests used as condition fixtures.
Do not infer campaign support from other global VM native registrations.

Campaign forms remain logical identities. Physical natives resolve PlayerRef to the campaign owner or an explicitly bound private reference copy; they never fall back to a shared vanilla reference. Explicit entry/recovery can materialize selected copies; automatic area-entry and full world coverage remain incomplete.

Alias getters support deterministic forced reference/location, unambiguous unique actor, and external-alias targets only. Alias-fill conditions, runtime fills, creation, propagation, lifecycle, reservations and alias effects remain unsupported.
Alias script variables and resolved bindings persist transactionally in VM schema 6. Getter support does not imply alias lifecycle or quest support.
Game.GetForm resolves owned static forms; dynamic forms require campaign allocation and are explicitly rejected.
Scene/TopicInfo.GetOwningQuest resolve owned metadata into the active campaign; dialogue/scene selection, execution and effects remain unsupported.

GetVMQuestVariable uses owned CIS2 and conditional PEX declarations in an adapter-enabled running quest. It reads private live/persisted numeric state; it does not initialize scripts or support dialogue/alias contexts.
UseGlobal comparisons resolve campaign globals before each stage log. Other special flags remain unsupported; all existing non-stage evaluation gates remain missing.

Placed-reference bindings merge owned base/reference properties and deterministic NPC templates. Variables persist in campaign reference roots. Transaction-generated inventory events run synchronously on these bindings and scripted active aliases; general world events, lifecycle, leveled templates and PlayerRef base bindings remain incomplete.

Strict method dispatch scopes self, typed receivers and Parent to the matching script chain. Missing native implementations, invalid inheritance and ambiguous script bindings fail. Unique ancestor casts are supported; dynamic script-handle identity, general lifecycle/events and durable latent calls remain incomplete.

Inventory GetItemCount/AddItem/RemoveItem support concrete base items, staged reads, extra-data-preserving transfers and synchronous OnItemAdded/OnItemRemoved handlers. FormLists, leveled/reference items, equipped-item removal, inventory-event filters, pickup UI messages and external pickup/drop/container-transfer event routing remain unsupported. Persistent inventory commits require atomic storage. Latent handlers fail and roll back the complete transaction.

Reference queries cover GetPositionX/Y/Z, GetAngleX/Y/Z (server degrees), Actor.IsDead, GetDistance, GetParentCell and GetWorldSpace. They require a transaction and registered campaign-owner/private-copy snapshots, validate full saved state, binding identity and phase at commit, reject nonfinite/overflowing spatial values, and never query a shared original. Distance requires one interior or worldspace. GetParentCell rejects a WRLD-only location without a campaign cell index; an interior GetWorldSpace returns None. These native methods do not add spatial condition-function support or live engine spatial/AI state.

IsDisabled plus Enable/Disable/EnableNoWait/DisableNoWait operate on validated bound private copies with staged read-your-writes. Mutation requires fade=false, no enable-parent/child links, no player target, no occupied reference, pending actor snippets/disable callbacks or respawn. Nonzero visibility changes commit with journal/VM/inventory state and an atomic save batch; latent execution, enable-parent propagation and engine fade behavior remain unsupported.

Visibility publication requires an explicitly installed projection barrier. Every connected assigned actor in the private phase must have a native packet epoch; shared-owner faction mutations include the owner and direct connected observers whose baselines contain that actor. Hosting an offline listener does not itself subscribe its host. All captured gates close before mutation and every token advances. Actor/connection lifetimes, observer membership and phase epochs are revalidated. Fresh manifests/baselines publish after subscription reconciliation; only their ordinary current-token ack may reopen gameplay. Abort/desynchronization quarantines captured connections; reused connection slots are protected. Native and JS callback receipts are synchronous, not durable disk acknowledgements.

Enabling a previously uninitialized copy can trigger its first subscription OnLoad transaction during postcommit reconciliation. A visibility mutation nested inside that load is refused by the active barrier. The outer visibility state has already committed; observers are quarantined rather than claiming rollback or playability. Defer/queue semantics for this lifecycle case remain unimplemented.

Native new-character gameplay is gated until a finite appearance for the assigned actor is accepted; projection control remains available. Binary decoding rejects truncated primitives/containers and mismatched constants. These transport and creation guards do not certify native character-creation completion, arbitrary loadout application or quests.

Self loadout restoration requires native player loadout API version 1. Canonical epoch/revision requests retain matching item instances, preflight future inventory/equipment intents, and observe each bounded native operation before further mutation. A global pending-effect barrier survives cancel, supersession and JavaScript reload; uncertain effects require confirmed world replacement. Settled jobs are terminal. The client requires native settlement plus two later matching observations, waits for a fresh baseline after projection/reload, and refuses temporary-enchantment loss in preview. Independent hand-spell changes are modeled; correlated spells, other selected-slot mutations and shouts remain unsupported. Ambiguous plain-stack operations, unsupported ammunition metadata, destructive changes to protected/unknown extras and oversized metadata additions are refused. Resource policies are 4096 stacks, 128 equipped copies, 1024 name bytes and 32767 items per mutation. Exact metadata allocation and mutations still need real-engine acceptance. This does not add server campaign natives or certify any quest.

Typed stage-log CTDA 35 GetDisabled and 47 GetItemCount require explicit Reference targets; 46 GetDead, 71 GetInFaction and 73 GetFactionRank also accept a nonnegative signed QuestAlias ID at byte 28 through existing owning-quest alias resolution. PlayerRef maps to the owner; other targets require bound private copies. Item counts use initialized transactional inventories, concrete base items (currently excluding keys), exact signed-int32-bounded counts and staged writes. Faction predicates use shared transactional rank and base-aware membership semantics, not a rank>=0 approximation. Static reference/item/faction record kinds are preflighted before OR; skipped branches do not resolve private copies or aliases. Implicit physical Subject/Target, evaluated empty or unsupported alias fills, nonactor actor predicates, special flags 0x1a and non-stage evaluation remain unsupported. Qualified selector features do not widen other function/context combinations.

The client native-array bridge uses declared native parameter types, typed empty/None arrays, strict element validation, a 65,536-element resource ceiling and current-update object-array wrappers. It does not add server campaign natives, durable latent continuations or real-game acceptance.

Faction native subsets require a registered campaign-owner or bound private actor and live FACT identity. Immutable template defaults do not mutate the live actor during reads or baseline publication; present complete snapshots including empty remain authoritative. Rank and membership are distinct: absence is -2, removal overrides are -1, active base membership survives other negative overrides, and player expulsion can yield -2 with membership true. New rank writes are restricted to [-1,127]; existing unique-actor removals require isolated base-layer modeling and are refused before commit. Raw SKSE GetFactions, faction crime/reaction mutations, alias faction effects and general engine event lifecycle remain unsupported. Changed factions commit and persist with journal, VM, inventory and visibility effects through the projection barrier. Saved signed byte ranks migrate exact legacy uint32-wrapped negatives; snapshots reject duplicate identities and more than 4096 rows. No quest is certified by this subset.

Client actor faction restoration requires native actor factions API version 1 and is experimental on the audited Skyrim 1.7.104 runtime. Complete snapshots include explicit factionId, rank and isMember. Native leases bind actor handles, base identity and world generation, preserve exact original ExtraFactionChanges rows and independent crime overrides, publish only per-reference rows, notify native faction/detection state and require two later distinct observations. Shared NPC bases are never mutated. Unrepresentable rank/membership pairs are rejected; active-base absence cannot be emulated by a -2 override. Native originals survive JavaScript reload and restore before actor disposal; confirmed world replacement supersedes old leases. Input, spawn and projection readiness wait for application/restoration, while stale revisions and failures cannot release them. Compilation and planner/transport tests are not real-engine acceptance or complete faction compatibility.

Settled native faction leases are sampled again on status requests after 30 Papyrus updates, with at most eight jobs processed per update. Drift closes readiness without rewriting the unexpected state. Restoration preserves current immutable-base metadata while restoring the original per-reference overrides. Pre-load suspends work but does not discard old-world handles, original visibility or uncertain native operations; an explicit postLoadGame success:false resumes cleanup and disconnects the invalidated session. Only confirmed world replacement permits forgetting old-world ownership. These policies have simulated lifecycle coverage, not engine acceptance.

Repeated stage execution honors owned DNAM AllowRepeatedStages only for an already-running quest and unambiguous selected stage. Every authorized repeat re-evaluates log conditions and fragments and advances the journal revision even if only an inventory reward changes; visited stages remain unique and highest stage stays monotonic. Sequential nested visits are allowed; active repeated-stage recursion requires asynchronous scheduling and fails atomically. QSDT completion precedes its fragment, preserves running, and retains active for Miscellaneous quests; repeated completion is a no-op. A stage with no log entries records visitation but returns false. The bounded lifecycle metadata parser retains exact flags, ordered stages, event IDs and scoped dialogue/story conditions. Parsing startup/shutdown/run-once metadata does not implement those lifecycles. Start/Stop/Reset and durable latent completion remain unsupported; raw state-only journal commands are not substitutes. No quest is certified.

Explicit nested checkpoints preserve receiver/scope, attachment/function identity, method/static/Parent/property call positions, one shared budget and typed locals in VM schema 6. Restore preflights every saved caller before running the leaf. Executable metadata is guarded by streamed SHA-256; caller-only arrays remain roots and shared array identity survives reload. The bounded codec migrates only valid old schema 5 leaf nodes. Candidate put/take is fail-atomic; taking consumes a pending scope/token once within that heap. Pending stacks prevent raw quest reset until cancellation semantics exist. Native C++ caller suspension and ordinary strict promises remain rejected. The experimental durable coordinator uses this entry path with saved stage/log work; production native waits, latent event cursors and lifecycle semantics remain required. No latent native or quest receives a new support claim.

AtomicDurable campaign transactions seal immutable owner/effect save batches before notifications and require atomic storage with per-submission results. Process-local receipts identify the campaign, journal revision and sequence, becoming Durable only after a matching successful result is processed by a world tick. Failed attempts retain their exact snapshots; later saves wait in FIFO order. Stale/duplicate callbacks, unrelated storage failures and optional buffer recycling cannot acknowledge another batch. Admission bounds sealed batches and serialized-plus-vector payload accounting; absent or incompatible storage is refused before execution. Clear/destruction abandons pending receipts; an already submitted write can still commit and remains a drain barrier in a reused world. The experimental job coordinator adds saved stage/log work and checkpoint recovery; real outbox delivery, latent event cursors and lifecycle jobs remain required. Production quests do not yet use durable execution jobs and no quest is certified.

The experimental QuestJobRunner schema8 supports trusted Stage, Interaction and ReferenceLoad roots sharing one campaign heap and serial exact-receipt transactions. ReferenceLoad captures owner-only target identity/templates and sequences OnInit (reference scripts only), OnCellLoad and OnLoad (including running aliases), then inventory FIFO. Init completion and its permanent marker share one save; already initialized references durably skip Init and repeat later load events. One live load root per canonical target prevents overlapping initialization. Handler waits, native children, state selection and aggregate budgets persist. After initialization, independent interactions may wake later load handlers; callback completion is not a universal interaction eligibility lock. Schemas1-7 migrate. Current schema10 limits are live128/stage16, completed numbered32, legacy256 and journal8MiB; older schemas retain their historic limits. Production subscription/load occurrence identity, durable deferred trigger ingress, pre-initialization reentrancy, stable packet action admission, atomic default world/player-inventory effects, causal notification outbox release, quest lifecycle/alias filling/cancellation, dialogue/scenes, game-calendar waits, client integration and real quest/performance validation remain unfinished. No quest is certified playable.

Nested world restoration reconstructs spatial membership and trigger occupancy without publishing load/movement events. Pending subscriptions promote on real refresh or movement, preserving occupancy; failed/reentrant publication retains retry state and native identities. Ticks, timers, save flushes, quest pumping and lazy chunk discovery pause inside restoration. Live spatial overwrite with published relationships is rejected; unchanged-spatial metadata application retains relationships. This is not durable event ingress, native initialization gating or a hot-world rewind protocol. No quest is certified playable.

Schema9 trusted native ingress atomically associates captured OnTriggerEnter/OnTriggerLeave occurrences with numbered Interaction jobs. Independent exact admission receipts prevent later handler or retirement work from revoking acceptance; retained retries compare immutable captures and compacted retries are opaque consumed acknowledgements. One campaign ingress stream has canonical bounded sparse retirement with exact retained/retired coverage. Schemas1-8 migrate without native occurrences. NextOccurrence is prospective; CaptureOccurrence does not change occupancy. Live movement, packet forwarding and load subscription routing remain separate until physical producer acceptance is atomic. Native initialization/load/reset policy, other event kinds, client integration and full quest/performance validation remain unfinished. No quest is certified playable.

Production movement admission rejects nonfinite numeric fields before effects, separates authorization from publication, validates actor/connection/phase/authority after callbacks, and guards against same-transform nested packet supersession. Movement is forwarded after state updates using checked recipient identities. The existing one-shot teleport correction remains. These changes do not make physical movement, occupancy and event capture atomically durable, add native event ordering/lifecycle, or certify complete quests or 32-player performance.

Atomic trusted occurrence batches admit up to64 contiguous Enter/Leave/OnTrigger captures with initial recipient snapshots and one exact save receipt; no handlers run during admission. Schema10 separates128 nonterminal roots from32 completed numbered results; completion retirement preserves the just-finished result, and schemas1-9 keep historical validation. Existing scheduler execution budgets remain bounded. This trusted backend API does not yet atomically accept physical movement/occupancy or release packets on save receipts, establish native event cadence, or certify any complete quest or multiplayer latency.

Stable-roster campaign movement now prepares source pose, persistent primitive occupancy baseline, and all Enter/Leave/OnTrigger captures in one durable admission; guest source saves preserve personal inventory/journal. Packets own their bytes and wait for the exact receipt, with per-send identity, authority, epoch and baseline checks. Transient flags apply at admission; ticks cannot reenter publication and quest execution. First enrollment uses old-position geometry; later samples require the saved baseline. Same cell/grid, upright initialized primitives and published stable subscriptions are required; unsupported enrolled spatial/visibility/roster paths are refused. Restored pending subscriptions, cell/grid/phase/teleport transitions, guest-hosted NPC context, general native cadence and production throughput remain unfinished. Transaction-local immutable job snapshots reduce repeated decoding without replacing external/final validation. No complete quest or player-count target is certified.

Journal-owned native admission preflights copied pristine roots and computes retention once, then exposes only immutable pristine/validated root snapshots to guards and owned-copy getters. A private Runtime success handshake freezes each actual first recipient capture; fabricated results, swallowed capture failures, post-capture roster changes, retained output identity swaps and generic job/gameplay mutation are rejected. Per-root whole-state setter serialization is replaced by assembled batch publication; independent initial/final state, heap, retirement and physical read validation remains. Both admission APIs enforce staged movement event count/order/name and physical source/target association. The legacy synthetic callback API otherwise remains trusted, with strict SetJobState validation. This does not add recovery publication, spatial lifecycle transitions, native cadence, dialogue/scenes, complete quests or a certified multiplayer performance target.

Explicit external capture contexts own validated jobs, initialization membership and exact journal bytes, pin actor/owner lifetimes and phase epochs, and reject stale campaign or content mapping state. Batch capture shares one context without reserving occurrence identities; scalar capture creates a fresh context per call. Each movement-plan reconstruction creates its own fresh context, while active journal transactions borrow current initialization state. Endpoint registration, binding uniqueness, template and physical validation remain live; no persistent cache or validation pass is removed. This optimization does not certify production multiplayer throughput, restoration/reconnect, spatial lifecycle transitions, complete quests or client playability.
